Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
1040 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A Heat Advisory is in effect Tuesday afternoon for all of
  Southeast Texas. Advisories will likely be needed daily
  throughout the work week as dangerous heat persists with high
  temperatures in the upper 90s/100s and heat indices in the
  106-112F range. 

- Patchy fog possible during the early to mid-morning hours for at
  least the next few days.

- Notable rain chances look to return over the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1040 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

Oh I see you're back for another installment of us telling y'all 
that it's hot! Whelp, pull up a chair, fill up your water bottle, 
and turn down the A/C, I've got a good one in store for y'all! I'm 
gonna keep it 100 with y'all...is what Mother Nature told me is 
ahead for tomorrow...and the next day...and the next day...and the 
next day...and the next day. After that things become a little bit 
uncertain because we have a return of notable rain chances over the 
weekend! Before that though, we gotta get through the heat
discussion. I know some will say well it's always hot in the 
summertime, but let's talk about why this is a little more notable
than our "typical" summer heat.

The 596-598 dam mid-level high (the heatdome) has nudged its way 
into northern TX where it'll remain through at least Thursday. 850mb 
temperatures will gradually increase each day above the 90th 
percentile and near 99th percentile at times. The upper level high 
pushing this anomalously warmer air aloft down to the surface forces 
it to compress and warm even further, which is how we'll get to 
these above normal temperatures for most of the work week. College 
Station, The City of Houston, and Houston/Hobby have only seen 100+ 
degree temperatures once this year...there is decent potential that 
we'll be tacking on a couple more occurrences to that stat. So, high 
temperatures in the upper 90s to low 100s through the work 
week...and we haven't even talked about the humidity yet. 

Winds at the surface will vary between southwesterly and southerly, 
which will help keep dew points elevated (low to mid 70s) closer to 
the coast. Further inland, we should see dew points mixing out into 
at least the upper 60s to low 70s in the afternoons through the work 
week. The air temperatures will be high enough though that heat 
indices will peak near or above the Heat Advisory threshold (greater 
than 108 degrees) daily beginning Tuesday. As a result, a Heat 
Advisory will go into effect Tuesday afternoon from 12pm-7pm for all 
of Southeast Texas (except the barrier islands). This will likely be 
extended through the end of the work week as we continue on a streak 
of dangerous heat. To give you an idea of how this week will play 
out...the Heat Advisory starts on Tuesday, and that's not even the 
hottest day of the week. Thursday through Saturday looks to be the 
peak of the heat. There won't be much relief overnight with low 
temperatures mainly in the upper 70s to low 80s. The atrocious 
humidity overnight will result in occasional rounds of patchy fog in 
the early to mid morning hours for at least the next few days. 

Let's end this discussion on a more hopeful note. In the first 
paragraph we discussed that there's some potential for rain over the 
weekend. Rain chances will be slim to none for most of the work week 
with PW values hovering between the 10th (~1.36") and 25th 
percentiles (~1.60"). Towards the end of the work week, the heatdome 
begins to retreat westward, which opens the door for our an upper 
level trough pushing through the eastern CONUS over the weekend. 
We've been keeping tabs on ensemble guidance over the past few days 
for surface low pressure development in association with this 
trough. There is fairly decent agreement on surface low pressure 
developing somewhere around the Mississippi River Valley Friday into 
Saturday. The exact placement is still uncertain and that matters 
because there will be an associated frontal boundary. Will this 
front be progressive? Well it's the summertime, so probably not. 
Will the front push through our area? Same answer. Where will the 
front stall? Who knows! However, it is something worth monitoring 
since convergence along the front does increase moisture in our 
area...thus the rain chances returning! Until then though, we'll 
have to make it through the triple digit heat.

With heat indices expected to at or above Heat Advisory criteria 
over the next several days, please keep heat safety at the top of 
your minds for any plans that you make (especially if outdoors). 
Know the signs of heat-related illnesses, stay hydrated (with 
water), take frequent breaks from the heat, wear loose/light-colored 
clothing and sunscreen, and ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS LOOK before you 
LOCK your vehicle. Don't forget about your pets as well! If the 
ground is too hot for the palm of your hand, then it is too hot for 
their paws. 

Batiste

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 623 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

VFR and south flow should prevail through the evening. We're
expecting a smattering of reduced visibility and low ceilings 
across the region late tonight/early tomorrow morning. Visibility 
restrictions should be slightly less expansive than earlier this 
morning due to slightly stronger winds within the top of the 
cloud-bearing layer, but there is still a 30-40% chance of
localized high-end MVFR visibility restrictions across the 
"central portions" of our forecast area (impacting the UTS, CXO, 
and LBX TAF sites).

Low ceilings/stratus should be thin and ragged instead of a dense 
blanket and generally build from SW to NE across Southeast Texas 
from about 8-16Z tomorrow morning. Most TAFs carry an additional 
line for a FEW-SCT block of lower clouds, with only CLL, UTS, and 
CXO carrying a ceiling in the current TAFs. However, there is a 
20-40% of at least short-lived MVFR ceilings at all TAF terminals.

All stratus should lift and scatter into a VFR Cu field in the mid 
to late morning, with south-southwest flow around 10 kts prevailing
at all terminals in the afternoon.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1040 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

A period of benign marine conditions continues with light to 
occasionally moderate southerly/southwesterly winds and 2-4 ft seas 
prevailing through the week. Increasing southwesterly winds over the 
weekend may prompt the issuance of caution flags.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
628 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat is expected this week with temperatures in the 
  upper 90s to 100s and heat indices of 106-110F. 

- A Heat Advisory is in affect today for the eastern parts of the
  forecast area. An area wide Heat Advisory is in effect for
  Tuesday.

- Later in the week, upper ridging begins to lose its control
  overhead, allowing temps to moderate slightly and rain chances 
  to return to the forecast.
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Sunday)
Issued at 1218 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

Over the next several days, heat will be our main concern as 
temperatures rise into the upper 90s, while the heat index pushes 
well above 100F. Heat advisories are in effect this afternoon and
Tuesday. For this afternoon, the advisory covers Acadiana and 
areas along I-49. For Tuesday, the entire region will be under a 
heat advisory, with forecasted heat index values up to 109F. This
hot weather is due to a robust upper-level ridge centered over 
the Four Corners region that extends across the southern US. This 
ridge will continue to create sinking air, leading to mostly clear
skies and keeping rain chances basically at zero through the 
middle of the week. The main limiting factor to the heat across 
the region will be afternoon mixing of dry air aloft down to the 
surface, lowering dew points and the heat index. For the next few 
days, the heat will be dangerous; if you are outside, make sure to
take plenty of breaks and stay hydrated.

The forecast will begin to change on Thursday as the ridge begins
to weaken and rebuild farther west. As the ridge weakens, we will
see a small increase in PoPs as a series of weak troughs rotate
around it. With less subsidence, we will also see more cloud cover
and possibly a few diurnally driven showers and storms on Friday
and through the weekend. 

&&

(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 609 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

High pressure regime will remain in control of the forecast over
the TAF period. VFR conditions as well as southerly winds will
prevail. There may be a brief period of light ground fog, but this
is anticipated to be contained to central LA.

11/Calhoun

High pressure will keep winds onshore between 5 and 10 knots.
Waves will be below 3 feet for the rest of the work week.

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1218 PM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

A few fires have formed across the region, mainly in Cameron
Parish, where fuels dry out quickly. A lack of wind will keep the
fire danger low. Minimum RH values will be around 50%, with max RH
recovery around 90%.
